findings.title: Port-8000 section asserts the owner's incident is three events without support for the identity
findings.evidence: Note 3.1 intro equates 000142's 'port-8000 conflict noted mid-session during the workbench builds' with three events; 000142 was created 2026-09-11T23:09, one row predates it as a demo rehearsal and one postdates it; the 09-11 record the triage annotation names is cited only in 3.2; SESS-2026-09-10-04 and SESS-2026-09-11-05 are listed as port-8000 sources but not used in the body.
findings.consequence: R17 is met by citation, but the claim that these are the event the owner meant is stated as fact; the 09-11 workbench-build occurrence may be unrepresented.
findings.minimal_fix: Say these are the recorded collisions found and that which one 000142 means is not established, or cite the 09-11 record in 3.1.

findings.title: 'Anchored pattern' offered as a fix for self-matching pgrep is not one
findings.evidence: Note 5.2 lists `node.*vite --port 5180` as an anchored pattern. Run: bash -c 'echo "pat: $(pgrep -f "node.*vite --port 5180" ...) self=$$"' printed 'pat: 14755 14761 14763  self=14761', so it matches the invoking shell's own pid.
findings.consequence: phase-arch-12 may treat it as a safe selector for a kill; head -1 takes the lowest pid, not the right one.
findings.minimal_fix: Drop it from the list or state that only exact argv comparison is safe and head -1 suits reads only.

findings.title: Wrong cross-reference to the command list
findings.evidence: 'How to read the evidence' says 'Section 9 lists the commands'; section 9 is the question table, the recipe is section 10.
findings.consequence: A reader following the pointer lands on the wrong section.

findings.title: Sources table lists records and an idea never used in the body
findings.evidence: SESS-2026-09-10-04, SESS-2026-09-11-05 and idea 000144 each appear once, in the Sources table only.
findings.consequence: Provenance overstates what was used; the findings the table credits to them cannot be checked in the text.
findings.minimal_fix: Cite them in the body with what they show, or remove them from the table.

findings.title: 000099 framed as the best account of PTY reaping though it shows an environmental shell-exit stall
findings.evidence: Note 3.3 intro says the investigation is 'the best account of how a PTY child fails to be reaped on time'; the 000099 coordinator finding and 000129 body attribute the failure to the pyenv shim lock stalling shell exit, with posix.py cleared; the note later concedes reaping was never part of it.
findings.consequence: Opening sentence can mislead phase-arch-12 into treating 000099 as reaping evidence; the facts are otherwise stated correctly.
findings.minimal_fix: Reword the intro to say a shell failed to exit in time for an environmental reason and that reaping proper is covered in 4.4.

findings.title: Section 7 leans toward a position on the kill-action tension
findings.evidence: Point 2 names a candidate repo-bounded boundary; point 6 ends 'The tension is therefore about the documented posture ... not about the capability being new to the host'; Q1 and Q6 repeat the cwd/argv signals.
findings.consequence: Nothing is decided and the section says so, but these sentences nudge phase-arch-12's own ADR toward permit-scoped-to-repo.
findings.minimal_fix: Present the boundary as one of several unranked candidates or cut point 6's closing sentence.
